item.title: Top 4 Reasons Why Python's math.ceil and math.floor Functions Return Floats Instead of Integers
item.description:
In this post, we delve into a particularly intriguing feature of Python’s math module: the way the math.ceil and math.floor functions return floating-point numbers instead of integers. This topic has sparked considerable discussion and sometimes confusion among users, especially those transitioning from other programming languages or backgrounds.

What Are math.ceil and math.floor?

According to the official Python documentation:

  • math.ceil(x) returns the ceiling of x as a float—the smallest integer value greater than or equal to x.
  • math.floor(x) returns the floor of x as a float—the largest integer value less than or equal to x.

This leads to the fundamental question: Why do these functions return float values when their primary intent is to determine integers?
